record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal carrying the traces from Theorem 2.8. Determine whether every trace on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces given by Theorem 2.8.

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8. ... This rule yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞}.
Problem 14. Show that on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} there exist no other traces than those provided by Theorem 2.8.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ range over all (complex) Banach spaces. For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to X$, recall the approximation numbers
$$a_n(T) := \inf\{\|T-A\| : A \in \mathcal{L}(X,X),\ \mathrm{rank}(A) < n\}, \qquad n=1,2,\dots,$$
and the Weyl numbers
$$x_n(T) := \sup\{ a_n(T B) : B \in \mathcal{L}(\ell_2, X),\ \|B\| \le 1 \}.$$

Fix $1 \le r < \infty$. The Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal $\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}$ consists of all operators $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,X)$ (over all Banach spaces $X$) such that
$$\sup_{n \ge 1} n^{1/r}\, x_n(T) < \infty.$$

For an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, let $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ denote the component obtained by intersecting with the Lorentz–approximation ideal
$$\{T : \sup_n n^{1/r} a_n(T) < \infty\},$$
i.e. operators in $\mathfrak{A}$ whose approximation numbers also satisfy $a_n(T) = O(n^{-1/r})$.

It is known that on the ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ there exists a family of (continuous, unitarily/ideal) traces obtained as follows: for each generalized limit $\mathrm{Lim}$ on $\ell_\infty$, the rule
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}(T) := \mathrm{Lim}_{N\to\infty}\, \frac{1}{\log N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} \lambda_n(T)$$
(where $\lambda_n(T)$ are the eigenvalues of $T$ arranged in non-increasing order of modulus, with multiplicities) defines a trace on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Question. Prove that every trace on the operator ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is of the above form; equivalently, show that there are no traces on $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ other than those induced by generalized limits via the eigenvalue Cesàro–logarithmic averaging rule.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the setting of traces on operator ideals over arbitrary Banach spaces. While trace-uniqueness questions on ideals of operators on Hilbert space have been studied extensively (e.g., Kalton's 1987 result showing the operator trace is not unique on proper subideals of trace class), no published resolution of the uniqueness question for the specific Banach-space ideal $(\mathfrak{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Operator Ideals with a Trace - Pietsch (1981)
status_evidence.snippet: Pietsch's foundational work on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Background on trace constructions for operator ideals; no uniqueness statement for the specific Lorentz–Weyl ideal in question.

status_evidence.title: Singular trace - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Kalton (1987) answered a question of Pietsch by showing the operator trace is not the unique trace on quasi-normed proper subideals of the trace class.
status_evidence.claim: Related trace-uniqueness questions in the Hilbert-space setting; no resolution stated for the Banach-space Weyl ideal.
